findings.summary: The remote AuthZ scope map is not extended with the two new governed operations, so a remote-surface principal (build_remote_app path) always gets FORBIDDEN 'operation is not mapped to any scope' for wf_evidence_put / wf_evidence_migrate. This is fail-closed and the systemd service path (server.main -> mcp.run) is unaffected, so it does not block the spec's acceptance, but the remote surface cannot exercise the new landing entry point until _MUTATE_OPS is extended.

Spec §3 states '不改 kernel', yet the fix adds DomainBinding.extra_runtime_state_paths, a keyword-only bind(runtime_state_paths=...) argument, and threads it through _validate_runtime_configuration/_runtime_state_allowances. The change is additive and opt-in (default empty, no scope/reconcile/ledger-schema/manifest semantic change, only work-folder passes a value) and is the minimal way to satisfy both spec §3's 'runtime state 写，参照 manifest/ledger 同门 runtime 路径' and the prior final-review blocker about the unregistered ignored-runtime allowance; §4 likewise only forbids kernel transaction-reliability changes. Recorded as a deviation from the literal non-goal, not as a correctness defect.

The runtime-payload restore on mutation failure is unconditional, but kernel.mutate can fail after the Git commit is already durable (runtime-state finalization raises MutationBrokenError post-commit). In that narrow BROKEN window the committed evidence/<filename>.sha256 pointer survives while the runtime original is rolled back to its prior bytes (or unlinked), so the pointer is not sha256-recomputable until the BROKEN mutation is manually recovered. The scene is preserved and the payload is regenerable, so this is a recovery-ergonomics gap rather than data loss.

The idempotent replay path returns the stored success response without re-materializing the runtime artifact, so a replay after the runtime original was deleted reports ok with a runtime_path that no longer exists. Consistent with mutation-ledger replay semantics for a regenerable artifact, but the reference-integrity check of spec §5.3 would fail for that path until the artifact is re-put.

The reference file is named evidence/<filename>.sha256, so pointer commits still literally match the frozen §5.2 acceptance glob '**/audit-evidence*'. The spec's own suggested reference name ('audit-evidence-<t>.ref') has the same property, so §5.2 must be read as 'no new commits carrying the bulk originals' — which the implementation satisfies (only pointer-sized files are committed; originals land ignored under .katana/runtime/evidence/). Flagged so the Ops verification run does not read a non-empty git log as a regression.
